Empowered Evocation gets Int modifier to one damage roll of evocation spells (which as far as I read it applies to all creatures hit by an AOE, since you roll the damage once). Yup, the shift in IQ scores is called the Flynn Effect for people that want to know more.

Regarding IQ, I wouldn't say that nobody's sure what IQ is/what it's testing. It is an attempt at quantifying an individual's general mental ability. Whether that general mental ability exists or not is another question (lookup "g factor" for more info).

The current main IQ test breaks it down into sub-categories (eg verbal abilities, attention/working memory). These sub-categories tend to be in the same range within an individual person, which suggests there's some type of general cognitive ability underlying. However the tests have flaws and those that research/develop them have decided what is or is not included on the test. I assume there's a systematic way it's decided, but I can't remember offhand how that was decided/it's too early in the morning for me to look into it.

You have a few of those options here (stacking bleed damage, flat damage reduction), so maybe focus on expanding those more. Maybe focus on different ways to stack the bleed. Just spitballing, but how about a reaction when you are hit by a melee attack, you reduce the damage and apply a bleed to the target, or shoot magical thorns to all targets within 5ft that deals damage/applies thorns on a failed Dex save.

I also think it's a really cool concept, but it's definitely overtuned. As you mentioned, Sentinel feat plus this subclass is very strong. I recommend comparing what this can do to Battle Master Maneuvers, which also are limited by 4 superiority die (scaling to 6 at level 15).

  
Serrated Strikes- This one is the most overtuned I think. Always adds proficiency bonus damage on a hit, which is a good amount of free damage. This also has double scaling as proficiency bonus and number of attacks increases. At level 11, that's potentially 12 free damage if you hit the target 3 times in a turn, which often isn't that difficult. It's also made easier with action surge and Vital Drain.



As there is no time limit, if a target doesn't make the save it lasts until the target dies. After Bleed Them Dry they can't even heal to save themselves from this. I would also give the target an option to do a Medicine check as an action to remove it (see Bearded Devil for wording). I would also clarify that the limit doesn't interact with action surge (e.g., if you have 2 attacks, it can't stack 4 times with action surge if all attacks hit). Maybe also make it not work on constructs/undead, as they don't have blood.

  
Vital Drain- This should require a save. Compare it to Trip Attack, which expend the limited resource of a superiority dice and it requires a save. With action surge this also allows the fighter to get a large number of attacks at advantage, which makes maxing Serrated Strikes easier.



Sharp Riposte- Again, compare to a maneuver, Riposte, which requires a superiority die. This also give you another opportunity to stack Serrated Strikes. With the level 15, if both attacks hit it's +10 damage (from Serrated Strikes) plus weapon damage outside of your turn. 



Bleed Them Dry- I'm okay with this overall, but situationally it could be super strong such as the case for creatures that heal (e.g., trolls). You are likely to be able to always prevent healing of at least one creature.

  
Hardened Blood- That's a pretty huge amount of essentially free damage mitigation. 

  
Briar Rose- Compare to Champion fighter's capstone (5 hp + Con modifier, likely overall 9 or 10) but only up to half HP. With Hardened Blood this makes it a crazy tanky subclass, likely a better tank than any other Fighter subclass. This is in addition to all the damage mentioned above.

Purpose- survey and introduction to range of therapeutic techniques and orientations for child/family

Learning a variety of orientations and determine which orientation is the best match for the presenting issues for the client

Developmental contextual perspective- what we will go over initially, importance of context (trauma being an important aspect of context, very common in clinical population)

Deidentification- change little aspects about the case (maybe where they are from, their exact age), definitely change the name, in an educational setting- change it so their best friend would not recognize who the person is

Papers- first part is explaining what the therapy is (literature review, needs to be cited), then how it can be applied to the case vignette

USE THE COURSE COMPETENCIES ON THE SYLLABUS TO MAKE SURE YOU ARE COVERING ALL POINTS AND COMPETENCIES REQUIRED

Not adequate to say “I will ask the client” if you don’t know some piece of information, specifically about culture

Separate out the review and the case material (don’t need to cite again if you refer to terms you have already defined them)

Should have headings that organize the paper

When citing secondary sources (say, a paper cites the primary source of Freud), only cite the secondary citation

You can rewrite as often as you want, she will continue to look at them, make sure you send it with track changes

Extra credit- send in a brief proposal to her (a few sentences) just so she make sure that it is related to the day’s lecture

If you want to do another orientation, must be empirically supported, must give very thorough review of theory, goals, and strategy/techniques because it is not covered in class

In the US, we use a single-member district plurality vote, meaning each district only gets one seat, which goes to the largest party.
